title: Calendar Bot Stops Guessing Norwegian Names Phonetically | vitalii.no
description:
How a growing SQLite vocabulary table stopped a speech-recognizer from phonetically mangling Norwegian place and school names every single time it heard them.

The calendar bot's speech recognizer used to transcribe Norwegian names the way they sounded, spelling Hoffsvangen skole or Utviklingssamtale out phonetically in Cyrillic — things like "Утвіклік-Самталє" or "Хоусваген Скуле". Every dictated event with a Norwegian name needed a manual correction before it could go on the calendar.

I added a vocab table with kind, canonical name, aliases and a note, seeded with real entries: place to Hoffsvangen skole, term to Utviklingssamtale, each with the phonetic variants the recognizer actually produced. A lookup function checks this table against the canonical name and its aliases before any phonetic guessing happens, normalizing case and diacritics. A learning function then grows the alias list automatically whenever a dictation gets corrected to a known name, refusing to let a new canonical entry be written in Cyrillic so the table only ever gets cleaner.

The result: a Norwegian name the bot has heard and been corrected on once is matched correctly from the vocab table every time after, instead of being mangled again.
